svg.text: FIG 04: SINGULARITY FUNCTIONS, IMPULSE JUMPS & DEGENERATE LOOPS
Dirac Delta Calculus • Charge & Flux Conservation Axioms • The 50% Energy Loss Paradox • Degenerate Traps

g.text: • Singularity functions model non-analytic, discontinuous circuit switching:
Dirac Delta: δ(t) = d/dt [u(t)], δ(t)=0 ∀ t≠0, ∫_{-ε}^{+ε} δ(t)dt = 1
Unit Ramp: r(t) = ∫ u(t)dt = t · u(t)
Key: Area of impulse = strength K. An impulse has infinite height, zero width, finite area.
∫_{-∞}^{+∞} f(t) · δ(t - t₀) dt = f(t₀) (if f is continuous at t₀)
f(t) · δ(t - t₀) = f(t₀) · δ(t - t₀)
Impulse Response h(t) vs Step Response s(t)
For a 1st-order series RC circuit excited by step V_s · u(t):
Step Response: v_C(t) = V_s · (1 - e^{-t/RC}) · u(t)
Impulse Response: h(t) = d/dt [v_C(t)] = (V_s / RC) · e^{-t/RC} · u(t)
• When an impulse δ(t) of current strikes a capacitor, or an impulse of
voltage strikes an inductor, state continuity is VIOLATED:
2. A loop formed ENTIRELY of capacitors and voltage sources?
3. A cut-set formed ENTIRELY of inductors and current sources?
If YES: Normal continuity v_C(0⁺)=v_C(0⁻) or i_L(0⁺)=i_L(0⁻) FAILS!
You MUST use Conservation of Charge or Conservation of Flux Linkage!
Consider C₁ charged to V₁ and C₂ charged to V₂. At t=0, switch closes
connecting C₁ in parallel with C₂ without series resistance (R → 0).
Conservation of Total Electric Charge Axiom:
C₁ · V₁ + C₂ · V₂ = (C₁ + C₂) · V_final(0⁺)
Consider L₁ carrying current I₁ and L₂ carrying current I₂ in series loop.
At t=0, switch closes placing L₁ and L₂ in series (or parallel cut-set).
Conservation of Total Magnetic Flux Linkage Axiom:
L₁ · I₁ + L₂ · I₂ = (L₁ + L₂) · I_final(0⁺)
(Sign depends on whether reference directions aid or oppose in the loop!)
What current actually flows during the transition t ∈ (0⁻, 0⁺)?
Since charge transfers instantaneously in zero time Δt = 0:
The current is an infinite-amplitude DIRAC DELTA IMPULSE!
Real switches always have stray resistance R_wire and inductance L_wire.
As R_wire → 0, peak current I_peak → ∞, but the energy dissipated
approaches a NON-ZERO CONSTANT INDEPENDENT OF R!
Initial State (t = 0⁻): C charged to V₀, uncharged C connected in parallel.
Final State (t = 0⁺): Charge splits equally Q₁ = Q₂ = Q/2, v(0⁺) = V₀ / 2.
Where did exactly 50% of the stored energy disappear to,
even if the connecting wires have ZERO RESISTANCE (R = 0)?
Answer: Lost as electromagnetic radiation (Poynting vector) and spark heat!
If series R is included, ∫ i²(t) R dt = ½ C V₀² regardless of R value!
Rigorous Proof: Independent of Resistance R
Let loop resistance be R. Current i(t) = (V₀ / R) · e^{-t / τ}, where τ = R · (C/2).
E_diss = ∫₀^∞ i²(t) · R dt = R · (V₀ / R)² · ∫₀^∞ e^{-2t / τ} dt
= (V₀² / R) · [ R · C / 4 ] = ¼ · C · V₀²
Notice that Resistance R CANCELS OUT COMPLETELY!
Whether R = 0.001 Ω or R = 1,000,000 Ω, exactly ¼ C V₀² is dissipated!
Smaller R simply means higher peak current for shorter duration.
General Master Formula: Arbitrary C₁, C₂, V₁, V₂
When C₁ at initial voltage V₁ connects across C₂ at initial voltage V₂:
Dual Inductor Formula: Arbitrary L₁, L₂, I₁, I₂
When L₁ with current I₁ is forced into series with L₂ with current I₂:
1. If V₁ = V₂, energy loss ΔE = 0 (no charge transfer occurs).
2. If V₂ = 0 and C₁ = C₂, ΔE = ¼ C V₁² = 50% of initial energy.
3. If C₁ = C₂ but V₂ = -V₁ (opposite polarity):
ΔE = ½ · (C/2) · [V₁ - (-V₁)]² = ¼ C · 4V₁² = C V₁² = 100% LOST!
Total charges neutralize each other completely! V_final = 0 V!
Drill 1: Impulsive Source across Parallel RC
Circuit: Current source i_s(t) = 5·δ(t) A in parallel with R = 2 Ω and C = 0.5 F.
Initial state: Capacitor uncharged, v_C(0⁻) = 0 V.
Step 1: Determine Jump in Capacitor Voltage at t = 0⁺
Current through resistor is finite, so all impulse enters capacitor:
For t > 0, impulse is zero (i_s = 0). Capacitor discharges through R:
Capacitor current i_C(t) = C dv_C/dt = 5·δ(t) - 5·e^{-t} u(t) A.
Two inductors L₁ = 2 H with I₁ = 6 A and L₂ = 4 H with I₂ = 0 A.
At t=0, switch closes placing them in series aiding loop.
λ_total(0⁻) = L₁ · I₁ + L₂ · I₂ = (2)(6) + (4)(0) = 12 Wb-turns
E(0⁻) = ½ L₁ I₁² + ½ L₂ I₂² = ½(2)(36) + 0 = 36 J
ΔE_loss = 36 - 12 = 24 J (Lost in arc across switch contacts!)
Drill 3: Impulsive Voltage on Series RL
Circuit: Voltage source v_s(t) = 12·δ(t) V in series with R = 3 Ω, L = 2 H.
Step 1: Jump in Inductor Current at t = 0⁺
Step 2: Time Domain Response for t > 0
Inductor Voltage v_L(t) for all t:
Resistor voltage v_R(t) = R · i_L(t) = 18 · e^{-1.5 t} · u(t) V.
Notice KVL holds at all times: v_L(t) + v_R(t) = 12·δ(t) = v_s(t)!
